newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - ScotPower eyes savings, strategy.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - ScotPower eyes savings, strategy.

text.p: British multi-utility Scottish Power Plc should see a rise in half-year profits when it reports on December 4 and is expected to give indications of savings and strategy following its takeover of Southern Water.

Pre-tax profits before exceptionals are likely to be between 175 million stg and 189.4 million, up from 127 million stg a year ago, with a dividend payout of around six pence per share, compared with 5.17 pence.

Analysts said exceptional charges could be around 40 million stg for restructuring after it bought water and sewerage company Southern Water for 1.68 billion stg in August following a battle with rivals Southern Electric.
It had already swallowed up electricity distributor Manweb last year, making it the first and only British company with generating assets allowed to buy a regional power company.
"The big issue for Scottish Power will be persuading shareholders that Southern Water was a good buy," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Scottish Power is expected to give details of cost savings expected from the merger and an outline of its strategy.
Along with water and electricity, the group has also got interests in gas and telecommunicatons.
"We will be eyeing the scope they give for savings in Southern Water," the analyst said.

The company's aggressive expansion strategy has left scant room for returns to shareholders in the form of special dividends or buybacks, analysts said, with gearing expected to be around 100 percent by the end of the year.
